findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler can no longer be instantiated (abstract methods unimplemented)
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`, but `StatefulDetectorHandler`/`DetectorHandler` declare four abstract members: `counter_names` (abstract property), `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Because none are implemented, `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(...)` raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...`. `Detector.detector_handler` instantiates the registered handler (`group_type.detector_handler(self)`), so any code path that touches a `metric_alert_fire` detector handler will now raise instead of returning an empty result list as it did before this change. mypy will not catch this since subclassing an ABC without implementing abstract methods is legal at definition time. Either keep a trivial concrete implementation or mark the class abstract and remove it from the registered group type until it's implemented.

findings.title: Stale TODO comment contradicts the code
findings.body: The comment "TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction" sits directly above a class that now *is* a `StatefulDetectorHandler`. Leaving it there is misleading for the next reader; it should be removed or replaced with the remaining work (implementing the abstract hooks).

findings.title: PriorityLevel(new_status) can raise ValueError for non-priority condition results
findings.body: `build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, PriorityLevel(new_status))` converts the computed status to `sentry.types.group.PriorityLevel`. `new_status` is derived from `max(new_status, condition.evaluate_value(value))`, and `DataCondition.condition_result` is DB/user-configured and not constrained to `DetectorPriorityLevel` values (it can be a bool or an arbitrary int). Any such value (e.g. `True` -> 1, or 10) makes `PriorityLevel(...)` raise an unhandled `ValueError`, aborting evaluation of the whole data packet (and leaving already-enqueued dedupe/state updates uncommitted). Validate/clamp the value, or only build an occurrence when `new_status` is one of the known `DetectorPriorityLevel` members.

findings.title: Occurrence fingerprint contract with build_fingerprint is neither enforced nor documented
findings.body: Resolution is emitted by the base class as a `StatusChangeMessage` whose fingerprint comes from `self.build_fingerprint(group_key)` (line 293), but the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook lets subclasses construct the `IssueOccurrence` fingerprint however they like, and the abstract method has no docstring stating that it must use `build_fingerprint(group_key)`. If a subclass picks a different fingerprint, the firing occurrence and the resolving status change will target different groups and issues will never auto-resolve. Document the requirement on the abstract method (or build/inject the fingerprint in the base class).

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but the docstring still reads "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Update it to describe the dict keyed by group key, otherwise implementers of the hook will be misled about the contract.

findings.title: get_group_key_values type annotation disallows the None group key that the code and tests use
findings.body: `get_group_key_values` is annotated `-> dict[str, int]`, but group keys are `DetectorGroupKey = str | None` everywhere else (`build_occurrence_and_event_data`, `get_state_data`, `build_dedupe_value_key`), and the new test `test_state_results` returns `{None: 6}` from this method. The annotation should be `dict[DetectorGroupKey, int]`; as written, type checking gives implementers wrong guidance about whether a `None` (ungrouped) key is allowed.

findings.title: get_state_data raises KeyError when a handler has no counters
findings.body: `counter_updates` is only populated inside `if self.counter_names:`; when a `StatefulDetectorHandler` subclass legitimately declares `counter_names = []`, `counter_updates` stays `{}` and `counter_updates[gk]` on this line raises `KeyError` for every group key, breaking all evaluation for that detector. Default to `{}` per group key (e.g. `counter_updates.get(gk, {})`).

findings.title: Expected occurrences are built with the wrong value, so value/priority propagation is untested
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group` the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with value `6` while the packet supplies `10` (similarly `TestEvaluate` builds expectations with `6` while packets carry `100`/`8`). The assertions still pass only because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` ignores `value`, which means the tests never verify that `evaluate_group_key_value` passes the correct `value` (or the correct `new_status`) into the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` hook. Make the mock occurrence depend on `value`/`new_status` (e.g. in `evidence_data`) and use the real values so a regression in the hook arguments would be caught. There is also no test that `process_detectors` produces a `PayloadType.STATUS_CHANGE` payload for the resolution path.
